title: Pregnancy Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Pregnancy Calculator: How many weeks pregnant you are today. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. How many weeks pregnant you are today. Enter your first day of last period and check on date and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Pregnancy is counted from the first day of your last period, so you're considered about two weeks pregnant at conception. This calculator shows your gestational age and trimester. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Pregnancy tools include [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator), [Ovulation Calculator](/ovulation-calculator) and [Pregnancy Weight Gain Calculator](/pregnancy-weight-gain-calculator).

## How to use the Pregnancy Calculator

Start by picking your first day of last period, then picking your check on date. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Pick your first day of last period.
2. Pick your check on date.
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Gestational age = date − LMP. Trimesters: 1–12 weeks, 13–26 weeks, 27+ weeks.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. With an LMP of 1 March 2026, on 1 June 2026 you would be 13 weeks 1 day — the start of the second trimester. Try the same figures in the [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (First day of last period: 2026-03-01, Check on date: today), the [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator) returns You are: 37 weeks 6 days, Trimester: Third, Due date: Sun, December 6, 2026, Days to go: 15. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Book your first prenatal appointment around 8 weeks.
- Start folic acid before or as early as possible in pregnancy.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why count from my last period?

Ovulation dates are rarely known precisely, while the start of a period usually is. Try it with your own numbers in the [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How long is a pregnancy?

About 40 weeks from LMP, or 38 weeks from conception. Try it with your own numbers in the [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Pregnancy Calculator use?

Gestational age = date − LMP. Trimesters: 1–12 weeks, 13–26 weeks, 27+ weeks. You can see it in action in the [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Pregnancy Calculator?

Just First day of last period and Check on date. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
